function: Learned Co-HDRL decides BS sleep modes and SBS transmit power levels for energy efficiency; RIS phase shifts use non-learned fractional programming (p. 4, p. 5, p. 9).
notes: Exclude, function. p. 4: "a Co-HDRL algorithm is presented in the following Section IV for sleep and power control, and then an FP-based algorithm is introduced in Section V for RIS phase-shift optimization." p. 5: the MBS meta-controller produces "high-level sleep control policies" and each SBS sub-controller "can adjust its transmission power level". p. 9: "an FP-based approach is applied to optimize RIS phase shifts". The learned part is BS sleep control (network management, above the PHY) learned jointly with terrestrial transmit power levels, so check 4 passes, but it designs no precoder, beam, or RIS phase shift, the only area-3 decision (RIS) being classical; none of the seven areas is solved by learning. Borderline: p. 1 calls BS transmit power plus RIS phase shifts "joint active and passive beamforming", but here only discrete per-user power levels are learned and the RIS (passive) part is FP, so I did not count it as area 3. If the reviewer regards terrestrial power control as radio resource management above the PHY, the code would be above_phy instead; the exclusion holds either way. The system has RIS and simulation results (p. 11-13), so checks 6 and 7 would not apply. The PDF (arXiv 2304.13226v2, 7 Jul 2024) prints no DOI but states acceptance by IEEE TCCN; Crossref gives this DOI the same title and authors.
